item.content:encoded:
Yeah yeah I know this was written in 2012, I just want to put some ideas out of my head.
After reading this, I thought, "Ok" and that's it. The climax (I'm assuming that that was the last addendum, right?) just didn't do much for me. I was thinking of how it could be spruced up a bit, and it occurred to me that by maintaining the thing, the foundation is sorta worshiping the broken god in a way, whether they like it or not. What if exposure to this thing sped up peoples' conversion to the CotBG? That would explain in part why there was such a big following popping up out of nowhere in the place where they found it. Of course, it's fun leaving that unexplained, but I think it would be more fun if the foundation had to deal with something insidious like what I suggested. Love me a good ol' ethical dilemma.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I don't personally see 217 as part of the CotBG, no. It could assist them greatly, yes, but coincidentally.

I see 808 like this; The CotBG is, in its current form, a collection of loosely associated cults something like the birth of Christianity in the Roman Empire. Yes, they're all worshiping the same God, but in secret. However, BECAUSE they're worshiping in secret, different sects may stray slightly from the original Methods.

The Church already knows that the Foundation holds 882 and 271. Some cults might attack the Foundation (like in the Man From Maple Street story), feverishly fighting to liberate the Heart of their god. Others might just passively grow in number. This particular cult, however, resided in France; the Western World's capital of culture and art. They felt they should make "other" preparations for their God's return. That they should build a musician to herald its coming.

It's not meant to be a weapon, no. As-is, it's basically a ~480m3, screaming scrap heap. But hey, 808 IS unfinished, after all. Is it a parade float? Perhaps. But I don't know if the 808 cult had more a plan past just making those machines sing.

Also, while writing this SCP, I began thinking "what if other cults exist that the Foundation's unaware of". I thought that idea could go somewhere, perhaps a story collection or a few more SCPs. Just saying- this isn't foreshadowing. Just an idea.

item.content:encoded:
I like this one. That being said, a few issues:

In the first and third paragraphs, you state that there in a human effigy atop it. I would get rid of the mention in the first paragraph; it's just redundant.

I feel like this one is cut off early:

  • Scary Robot, cool
  • Human effigy, cooler
  • Crazy shit happens when it isn't well maintained, awesome
  • Potentially lethal scream, slightly cliche but still cool
  • Crazy shit includes….machines turning on. Neat, now what do they do?
  • Run.
  • So?
  • …that's it.

See what I mean? You have a cool foundation but you don't quite build on it. At first I thought this was actually a giant automaton, and was expecting it to run around all giant or something, which would have admittedly been pretty cool (if a bit too Gundam-esque). Point is, you need to up the creep in some way. Withholding vote for now.

non-electronic machinery affected by this resonance will spontaneously start up on their own through unknown means.

Could shorten that to simply:

non-electronic machinery affected by this resonance will spontaneously activate.

Also, what constitutes non-electronic machinery? Devices with no electronic components whatsoever, or only the non-electronic components of such devices as have them?

I'm not sure how I feel about this one, all in all. It's definitely not bad, but the humanoid effigy feels tacked on and clashes with my personal image of the broken god and associated artifacts - that it and everything to do with it is distinctly inhuman.
